changes.title: A function put in between two parts, or taken out again, now shows as one fork step together with the line it replaced

how.words: Its fork pairing now counts new and gone lines as well as parts (commit:02ffe98, doc:docs/CHANGES.md), so a function slipped between two parts — or removed — comes out as a single step pairing the fork with the direct line it replaced, instead of separate part and line steps.

changes.why: So a structural edit like slipping `validate_order` between `create_order` and `orders-db` reads as one change with a clear before and after, rather than as scattered part and line steps (commit:02ffe98, doc:docs/CHANGES.md).
changes.check: Counting whole lines in the fork pairing can merge or split steps where a stretch mixes part edits with line edits — check such a stretch still comes out as the right fork steps.

changes.title: A step now shows its route before and after — as Before/After chains on the card, with the fork's shared parts lit plainly in the picture

how.words: `changes_walk` now calls the new `before_after`, which traces the step's lines into chains of parts (`docair-viewer.page_changes.routes`) and prints the names as code (`docair-viewer.page_changes.names_as_code`), so the card reads 'Before · create_order → orders-db' and 'After · create_order → validate_order → orders-db'; per commit:02ffe98 the same `changes_walk` edit also lights the fork's shared parts plainly and draws lit new lines solid green and gone lines dashed.

`sort_flow` now calls the new `line_ends`, which gives the two ends of a graph line by its id (`<from> -<kind>-> <to>`, with a label or `#2` after it) — the endpoint detail each of the step's lines is presented by.

changes.why: So a reviewer can read straight off the card how the route changed — for example a write moving from `orders-db` to `orders-queue` — and see in the picture where the change forks off and rejoins; a part whose tags changed what it calls is shown by its lines, not listed as a change in its words (commit:02ffe98, doc:docs/CHANGES.md).
changes.check: The Before/After chains are traced from the step's own lines, so check them against the real before and after graphs — especially where a part's tags changed what it calls, and where a step has no line to it (the doc's `audit` row shows Before as '—').
